{{Top}}
The '''Pirate's Code''' also known as the '''Code of Honor''' or simply '''Pirate's Honor''', was a standard of conduct practiced by some [[Pirate/Legends|Pirates]].<ref name="P&P">''[[Pirates & Privateers]]''</ref>

==History==
The Pirate's Code reached back centuries, though its adherence during any given era ebbed and flowed, but generally survived. The code developed as a survival mechanism; pirates who raided indiscriminately and slaughtered or [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] their victims tended to develop extremely large bounties and became priorities for law enforcement and governments. In comparison, those who favored stun weaponry, left their victims alive, focused primarily on cargo, and were personable and charming developed far smaller bounties and were much lower on the priority list of law enforcement and bounty hunters.<ref name="P&P"/>

==Characteristics==
While the exact code and specifics varied, broadly the Code embraced a lack of violence for violence's sake. Honor demanded that victim's be treated as fairly as possible, to the point that legends abounded of magnanimous pirate captains treating valiant victims to feasts of fine food before sending them on their way unharmed. Honorable personal combat and naval mettle were highly prized, with emphasis on stealing from the capable rather than the poor and defenseless. Even outright adversaries such as bounty hunters and law enforcement were covered by the code, and both the [[Sector Ranger/Legends|Sector Rangers]] and [[Corellian Security Forces|CorSec]] had reports of pirates sparing the lives of particularly determined or admirable officers out of respect. The Code also dealt with the interpersonal relations of pirates, especially [[Ship's Articles]], and the challenging of command through duels through the [[Rules of the Blade]].<ref name="P&P"/>
